candidates.name: Opposite-endpoint return map with self-supplied Kuratowski contraction -> aligned chords
paper_items: I15 contraction estimate chi(gH)<=(1-M/U)^2 chi(H) (eq:contraction, main.tex:269-291)
candidates.statement: At an attained maximal defect D_t(x0,y)=M>0, define g on directions v at ty: x(v)=ty+p v in S_X, f(x)=tb+s w, opposite contact f(z)=tb-u w, g(v)=(ty-z)/r. On E={s-p=M} extremality forces r=u+M, so ||g(v)-g(v')|| <= (up/rs)||v-v'|| + scalar terms with up/rs=(1-M/r)(1-M/s)<=(1-M/(1+t))^2<1; binning p,u gives chi(gH)<=gamma chi(H); Darbo on the invariant closed convex C (C2) yields a fixed direction = aligned chords x=ty+pv, z=ty-rv, f(x)=tb+sw, f(z)=tb-uw, s-p=r-u=M.

final.justification: The only item with no neighbour found in any field. The eureka content is that a hypothetical positive defect M manufactures the contraction margin (1-M/r)(1-M/s) that a Darbo argument needs, removing all compactness/finite-dimension assumptions that every prior approach relied on. Downgrade risks: (i) every component is classical (Darbo, radial contact, two triangle inequalities) and once the aligned-chord target is posed the fixed-point move may be one step away (arm A of P-C1); (ii) full texts of Tingley 1987 and Kadets-Martin 2012 could not be read, so a fixed-point/return argument there is not excluded; (iii) the device may be a one-off (downstream test). Not transfer: Darbo itself is N0 transfer; the candidate is the problem-specific map and its self-supplied contraction.

candidates.name: Extremal common-support propagation and the invariant convex face (hull growth)
paper_items: I11 extremal set E and propagation rule (eq:equality, main.tex:243-256)
I12 invariant closed convex set by strictly-positive hull growth (main.tex:258-267)
candidates.statement: For v in E: r=u+M and ||pv+r g(v)||=p+r, so v,g(v) share a support, and every unit l sharing a support with g(v) lies in E. Growing conv{v0..vn} by v_{n+1}=g(a_n) with strictly positive a_n keeps one common support equal to 1 on the hull, so C=clco{v_i} is a closed convex subset of E inside S_X with g(C) in C.
